summary: The specification has complete source traceability and no uncovered candidates, but it contains several duplicate requirements, inconsistent priorities, terminology inconsistencies, unresolved retention and scope issues, and multiple vague or non-testable statements.

issues.description: REQ-RPTMG-042 and REQ-RPTMG-044 both require support for report definitions in an appendix. They differ only in the appendix letter and do not define distinct system behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace them with one requirement that references the complete, versioned report-definition catalog, or expand each appendix reference into distinct, testable report capabilities.

issues.description: Both requirements specify the same consortium scale: 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and more than 900,000 items purchased and processed annually.
issues.suggested_fix: Retain one capacity requirement and remove the other, or distinguish system capacity from operational workload with separate measurable acceptance criteria.

issues.description: Both requirements require integration with the enterprise Library Automation System, including the Acquisitions and Cataloging modules.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge into one integration requirement and define the required interfaces, data ownership, and supported operations.

issues.description: Both requirements require filtering and grouping reports by age, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate into one patron-characteristic filtering and grouping requirement, retaining any additional patron-type detail in that requirement.

issues.description: The stale-holds and unfilled-holds requirements overlap substantially, and REQ-RPTMG-028 also lists both categories in its holds report catalog.
issues.suggested_fix: Define whether stale holds are a subset of unfilled holds. Use one requirement with explicit status definitions, or retain separate requirements with non-overlapping criteria.

issues.description: Both requirements provide counts of records edited during a specified period. One covers items and the other bibliographic records, but the shared concept and reporting behavior should be distinguished explicitly.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a common edited-record reporting capability with explicit record types, or clarify why item edits and bibliographic edits require separate reports.

issues.description: Both requirements require background report processing through a queue so reporting does not interfere with interactive or circulation work.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge them and include the caching requirement for the inactive-patrons report as a separate, explicitly scoped subrequirement if needed.

issues.description: Both requirements require separate development and training environments and migration of report configurations into production.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge into one environment and configuration-migration requirement, including the complete list of migrated artifacts.

issues.description: Both requirements require delivery of generated reports by email to entered or designated recipients.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the requirements and include recipient entry, multiple recipients, address-book selection, and delivery behavior in one requirement.

issues.description: Both requirements require real-time reporting and current data on demand, but they use different priorities and wording.
issues.suggested_fix: Define one real-time or current-data requirement with a measurable freshness target and consistent priority.

issues.description: Both requirements require complete data specifications describing records, fields, data types, and relationships.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge them and resolve the different scopes and priorities.

issues.description: Both requirements require accessibility for the system and reporting interface using assistive technologies. The coverage of applicable standards also overlaps.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge into one accessibility requirement, distinguishing system-wide obligations from interface-specific implementation details if necessary.

issues.description: Both requirements allow authorized staff to convert the status of multiple items in one batch, including changing missing items to discard/weed.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the requirements and assign the capability to the appropriate operational area.

issues.description: REQ-ACCT-002 and REQ-ANALY-009 require monthly and annual aggregates to be retained indefinitely, while REQ-ACCT-011 requires configurable retention periods, including seven years. The specification does not state whether indefinite aggregate retention overrides the configurable policy.
issues.suggested_fix: Define retention rules by data category, explicitly stating which aggregates are exempt from deletion and how legal holds or policy changes are handled.

issues.description: The specification requires a historical reporting warehouse while also discouraging denormalized reporting stores and requiring reporting isolation. These constraints can coexist, but the current wording does not define whether a warehouse, read-only replica, or normalized historical store is permitted.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify the permitted reporting architecture and state how historical data is synchronized, isolated, and kept consistent without violating the denormalization constraint.

issues.description: The specification uses branch, library, location, system, region, and consortium inconsistently for organizational entities. For example, REQ-LOCAP-010 uses branches, while REQ-CALCD-009 discusses branches and REQ-ANALY-006 compares libraries.
issues.suggested_fix: Use 'library' for a physical organizational unit, 'library system' for the collection of libraries in one administrative system, 'region' for a configured grouping of libraries, and 'consortium' for the participating library systems. Use 'location' only for an item or workstation location.

issues.description: The same person concept is called patron, user, staff, report user, and community engagement user. 'User' is also used for both authenticated staff and library patrons.
issues.suggested_fix: Use 'patron' for a library customer, 'staff member' for an employee, and 'report user' only when referring to an authorized staff role operating reporting functions. Add these distinctions to the glossary.

issues.description: The same consortium capacity need is assigned P1 in REQ-NFRQA-006 and P2 in REQ-NFRQA-027.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the duplicate and assign one priority based on whether the scale is a hard acceptance constraint or an important operational target.

issues.description: The same patron-characteristic filtering and grouping need is P2 in REQ-DATAQ-006 but P1 in REQ-STKID-014.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the requirements and use one evidence-based priority.

issues.description: Real-time reporting is P2 in REQ-ANALY-013 and P3 in REQ-NFRQA-019 even though both describe the same capability.
issues.suggested_fix: Define a single measurable current-data requirement and assign one priority.

issues.description: Complete data specifications are P2 in REQ-DATAQ-014 and P1 in REQ-NFRQA-007.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the requirements and resolve whether the documentation is mandatory for acceptance or merely important.

issues.description: Email report delivery is P2 in REQ-RPTMG-022 and P3 in REQ-RPTMG-041.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the duplicate requirements and assign a single priority.

issues.description: These requirements use untestable freshness terms such as 'immediately,' 'near real time,' 'real-time,' 'current,' and 'complete and current' without defining allowable delay, measurement point, or completeness criteria.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify measurable targets, such as maximum transaction-to-report latency, maximum data age, completeness rules, and the behavior when source data is unavailable.

issues.description: The requirements contain vague or unbounded terms including 'all gaps identified,' 'straightforward workflow,' 'high-level reports,' 'acceptable performance,' 'minimize long run-times,' and 'reliable outputs.' These cannot be objectively verified from the descriptions.
issues.suggested_fix: Define the specific gap list, user actions, report contents, response-time or throughput targets, and report accuracy or test criteria.

issues.description: These requirements depend on Appendix A, Appendix B, or an implied report catalog that is not included in the requirement text. They are therefore not self-contained or independently testable.
issues.suggested_fix: Include versioned appendix contents or replace the references with explicit report names, fields, filters, scopes, and output rules.

issues.description: Several domain terms are undefined or ambiguous. REQ-ACCT-005 contains the phrase 'forgive, work, and goods payments,' REQ-DATAQ-004 uses 'discard/weed' and 'time-in-status,' and REQ-PURGE-003 uses 'weeding' without defining statuses or business rules.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct the apparent wording error and define payment types, item statuses, status-transition rules, and the meaning of time spent in a status.

issues.description: DIS-013 discards C-065 as out of scope because it is a transfer-management feature, but transfer management is explicitly in scope and REQ-OPMIS-012 already requires identification of delayed transfers. If C-065 expresses alerts for delayed transfers, it is a valid additional requirement rather than an out-of-scope candidate.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore C-065 as a requirement if alerts are needed, or revise the discard rationale to state that only reporting—not proactive alerting—is in scope.

issues.description: DIS-002 discards vendor data integration as out of scope, yet retained requirements REQ-NFRQA-035 and REQ-DATAQ-024 explicitly require vendor APIs, file transfers, and optional EDI data. The discard rationale is inconsistent with the retained specification.
issues.suggested_fix: Either restore and consolidate the candidates as vendor-integration requirements or remove the retained vendor-integration requirements and update their sources and scope.

issues.description: Although automatic checks report no uncovered candidates, the specification lacks measurable acceptance targets for capacity, report execution time, queue behavior, data freshness, and interactive-system impact. These are important needs expressed in the sources and cannot be validated from the current requirements.
issues.suggested_fix: Add explicit performance and capacity requirements covering representative workload, concurrent users or jobs, maximum response and completion times, report freshness, and acceptable OPAC/circulation degradation.

issues.description: The requirements have document-level sources, but the referenced Appendix A and Appendix B content is not identifiable in the supplied document list or requirement text. This weakens traceability to the actual report definitions.
issues.suggested_fix: Add explicit source identifiers for the appendices or include the appendix content and version in the specification.

glossary.definition: A library customer whose account, demographic information, holds, or circulation activity may be represented in the system.
An employee or authorized worker who logs in to operate the system or use reports.
An authorized staff member who runs, designs, schedules, reviews, or administers reports.
A physical or administrative library unit that owns, houses, or manages items and is used as a reporting scope.
The administrative system containing one or more libraries that share operational data and reporting.
The broader group of participating library systems governed or operated together.
A physical or electronic library copy that can have a location, status, circulation history, value, or transfer history.
A catalog record describing a title or work and its bibliographic metadata, distinct from the individual items attached to it.
A recorded operational or financial event, such as a checkout, check-in, renewal, hold placement, payment, or registration.
A patron request for an item or title, including its placement method, status, fulfillment, and pickup state.
A set of selectable fields, filters, joins, grouping rules, and Boolean conditions used to retrieve or analyze records.
A generated presentation or export of queried, aggregated, or predefined system data.
A saved report definition containing fields, criteria, formatting, permissions, and optionally scheduling or delivery settings.
Library material tracked for inventory or circulation without a complete bibliographic record.
An authorized operation that permanently deletes selected records or related records from the system.
The collection-management process of identifying items for review, withdrawal, discard, or purge; it does not itself imply deletion.
